open_points.subject: Agent authorization to author flows
open_points.text: “the token says whether the agent may author”; “author a function contract or implementation | agent with author right”; “compose and prove a flow | agent”
open_points.question: Does the may-author right govern flow composition as well as function contracts, implementations and trial cases?
options: Only agents with the author right may compose flow versions
Every authenticated agent may compose flows, while the author right applies only to functions and trial cases
open_points.default_guess: Require the author right for composing flows.

open_points.subject: Owner identity and token lifecycle
open_points.text: “Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token.”
open_points.question: Who provisions, rotates and revokes the owner token, how is it distinguished from agent tokens, and what observable refusal results from a missing or invalid token?
options: Installation-managed single owner credential with explicit authentication refusals
Reverse proxy authenticates the owner and passes a trusted owner identity
Owner uses an ordinary token specially marked as owner
open_points.default_guess: Use an installation-managed owner credential and refuse unauthenticated requests with a distinct authentication result.

open_points.subject: Platform manifest trust
open_points.text: “Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest.”
open_points.question: Who supplies and may change the manifest, where the kernel reads it from, and whether its contents are trusted configuration or untrusted external input?
options: Protected installation configuration maintained by an operator
A platform service queried by the kernel
Repository data read and validated at startup or request time
open_points.default_guess: Treat the manifest as protected installation configuration and validate it before use.

open_points.subject: Repository boundary
open_points.text: “A second agent with the same access continues the work from the kernel's records, the platform manifest and the repositories alone.”
open_points.question: Which repositories exist, who can read or write them, and whether repository access is through the kernel or an independent agent trust boundary?
options: Repositories are outside the kernel and independently accessible to agents
The kernel exposes repository-backed artifacts through MCP
Repositories are deployment inputs available only to operators
open_points.default_guess: Treat repositories as external systems independently accessible to authorized agents.

open_points.subject: Agent access to microservices outside the kernel
open_points.text: “the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel, with its own access to the service that holds the photo”
open_points.question: What external channel, credentials and authorization allow an agent to access a microservice directly, and how does this coexist with the stated kernel-mediated operation boundary?
options: Agents may independently call selected service APIs with separate credentials
Photo processing is performed by an external owner-controlled tool, not the agent principal
Agents cannot call services directly and processing must be represented by a service operation
open_points.default_guess: Model direct agent-to-service access as a separate, explicitly authorized external trust boundary.

open_points.subject: Personal-data leakage through untrusted function behavior
open_points.text: “Agent-written code — untrusted forever”; “An agent never receives a personal_data value”
open_points.question: How are exceptions, stdout, stderr, timing, resource usage and success/failure results from agent-written code prevented from disclosing personal data to the authoring agent?
options: Suppress or classify all code-controlled diagnostics and observable results at the highest input class
Permit bounded diagnostics and accept the resulting side channel
Forbid personal_data from entering agent-written functions
open_points.default_guess: Classify or suppress every code-controlled observable at the highest input disclosure class.

open_points.subject: Secret-echo detection
open_points.text: “A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone”
open_points.question: Which secret representations and response locations are scanned, at what stage, and what observable run result replaces a withheld response?
options: Scan raw response bytes for exact configured secret byte strings and fail the node
Scan decoded textual fields and return a redacted validation failure
Withhold the body but let the node succeed with no output
open_points.default_guess: Scan raw response bytes for exact secret values, fail the node, and record a non-secret reason.

open_points.subject: Implementation submission and automatic admission
open_points.text: “author a function contract or implementation” and “admit and activate | kernel, when an implementation is submitted”
open_points.question: When valid code is stored but admission fails, is the implementation retained, and what single observable result does the submitting request return?
options: Retain the immutable implementation and return its identity plus the failed admission verdict
Refuse the entire submission and retain nothing
Retain it but return only the authoring result; admission is separately observable
open_points.default_guess: Retain the implementation and return its identity together with the admission verdict and reasons.

open_points.subject: Trial execution selection
open_points.text: “try an implementation | agent | trial evidence per case”
open_points.question: Which contract version, implementation and set of cases does a try request select, and may an agent without the author right try unadmitted code?
options: Request names an implementation and runs the whole current corpus; any agent may do so
Request names selected cases; only authoring agents may try
Try always runs the newly submitted implementation automatically
open_points.default_guess: Require an implementation identity, run the whole current corpus, and allow any authenticated agent to request it.

open_points.subject: Trial-case oracle
open_points.text: “add a trial case”; “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus”
open_points.question: What does a trial case assert—successful contract conformance only, exact expected values, expected failure, or another predicate—and how is equality evaluated?
options: Input plus exact expected outputs using canonical value equality
Input plus an assertion that execution succeeds and outputs satisfy schemas
Input plus declarative expected success, failure or output assertions
open_points.default_guess: Use declarative cases containing inputs and canonical expected outputs or an expected failure.

open_points.subject: Capturing failed executions
open_points.text: “the trial case every later implementation must pass”
open_points.question: What trial assertion is created from an execution that failed, given that the failed execution has no correct output to preserve?
options: Capture its input and require future execution to succeed with schema-valid output
Owner or agent must supply the expected output when capturing
Capture the input and forbid recurrence of the same failure code
open_points.default_guess: Capture the input and require future execution to succeed and conform to the contract.

open_points.subject: Runtime failure result of run
open_points.text: “a run of the flow's active version, with outputs, or resting awaiting_approval / pending”; “a failed node stops its dependants”
open_points.question: What does the run action observably return when a node fails, including when independent branches continue?
options: Return a run resource whose state later becomes failed after runnable branches finish
End the run immediately on the first failed node
Return partial outputs with per-branch status and a failed terminal run state
open_points.default_guess: Continue independent branches, then return a failed run with partial outputs and per-node trace results.

open_points.subject: Run terminal-state aggregation
open_points.text: “A failed node stops only its dependants.”
open_points.question: When one branch fails while other branches succeed or wait, when does the whole run become failed and which waiting or runnable branches remain active?
options: Continue every independent branch and become failed only when none can progress
Any failed node immediately ends the entire run
Continue runnable branches but cancel all waits once any node fails
open_points.default_guess: Continue independent branches and become failed once no node can progress and at least one required node failed.

open_points.subject: Cancelling an executing operation
open_points.text: “cancel a run | owner | the run ends cancelled; nothing further is sent”
open_points.question: What happens if cancellation is requested while a function or HTTP operation is already executing, and how is its eventual result recorded?
options: Cancellation prevents new work but cannot retract an in-flight send; its outcome is traced
Cancellation waits for the active execution to finish before ending the run
The kernel forcibly terminates functions and aborts HTTP requests where possible
open_points.default_guess: Stop scheduling new work, terminate sandbox work where safe, and trace any already-sent operation outcome without sending anything further.

open_points.subject: Standing-grant eligibility
open_points.text: “grant a standing approval for a node”; “a destructive node ... cannot be granted”; “each state-transition, external-effect and destructive node stops ... unless ... a standing approval”
open_points.question: May grants be created for read and draft-write nodes, or only for state-transition and external-effect nodes that otherwise ask for approval?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect nodes are grantable
Every class except destructive is grantable
Any operation node is grantable, even if the grant has no behavioral effect
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for state-transition and external-effect nodes.

open_points.subject: Reading an unknown trace
open_points.text: “read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —”
open_points.question: What happens when the requested run or trace does not exist or the caller is not authorized to see its values?
options: Refuse with unknown-reference or authorization reason
Return an empty collection
Return metadata with protected values replaced
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unknown references and apply disclosure filtering to existing traces.

open_points.subject: Effect-class authority
open_points.text: “Effect classes are read, draft-write, state-transition, external-effect, destructive.”
open_points.question: Who assigns an operation's effect class, where it is stored, and what prevents an agent from proposing a harmful operation as read or draft-write?
options: The trusted platform manifest assigns the class and bindings merely pin it
The agent proposes the class and the owner accepts it with the binding
The kernel derives the class from HTTP method or another fixed rule
open_points.default_guess: Require the trusted manifest operation record to declare the effect class, which the accepted binding pins.

open_points.subject: Operation-to-HTTP request mapping
open_points.text: “An operation binding gives one manifest operation typed input and output ports”; “the fully built request ... method, URL, headers and body”
open_points.question: Where and by whom is the deterministic mapping from typed inputs to HTTP method, URL, headers, body, target and response output defined and validated?
options: The manifest operation record contains a declarative mapping pinned by the binding
The proposed binding contains the mapping and owner acceptance trusts it
Kernel code contains a service-specific adapter
open_points.default_guess: Put a declarative request and response mapping in the pinned manifest operation record.

open_points.subject: Operation response validation and failure
open_points.text: “their answers are untrusted data until validated at the port”
open_points.question: Which HTTP statuses, content encodings and schema violations constitute node failure, and what bounded non-secret result is exposed when validation fails?
options: The manifest declares accepted statuses and decoding; all other responses fail validation
Every 2xx response is decoded against the output schema
Bindings define response-status and decoding rules
open_points.default_guess: Have the pinned operation record declare accepted statuses and decoding, then fail the node with a bounded sanitized reason on mismatch.

open_points.subject: Idempotency-key declaration
open_points.text: “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key”
open_points.question: Who declares whether and where an operation accepts an idempotency key, how the key is generated, and what happens when an effectful operation has no compatible key location?
options: The trusted manifest declares key placement and every effectful operation must support it
The binding declares key placement subject to owner acceptance
The kernel always supplies one standard HTTP header
open_points.default_guess: Require every effectful manifest operation to declare key placement and derive a stable key from run and node attempt identity.

open_points.subject: Sandbox resource ceilings
open_points.text: “typed ports and resource bounds”; “bounded time, memory, output and processes”
open_points.question: What installation-level ceilings constrain author-declared resource bounds, and what refusal occurs when a contract requests more?
options: Fixed installation ceilings validated when the contract is authored
Kernel-wide constants compiled into the implementation
Owner acceptance is required for bounds above defaults
open_points.default_guess: Validate contract bounds against protected installation-wide maxima and refuse excessive contracts.

open_points.subject: Python execution target
open_points.text: “Functions are written in Python only”; “the Python standard library only”
open_points.question: Which Python implementation and version, module allowlist, source encoding and callable interface form the stable contract for implementations?
options: One installation-pinned CPython version with an explicit module allowlist and entry-point ABI
Any supported Python 3 version using the whole standard library
A kernel-defined restricted Python subset independent of CPython version
open_points.default_guess: Pin one CPython version and define an explicit entry-point ABI and standard-library allowlist.

open_points.subject: Schema vocabulary and equality
open_points.text: “Every port carries a value schema. An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.”
open_points.question: What schema language is used, how schemas are canonicalized, and whether “same” means byte identity, canonical structural equality or semantic equivalence?
options: Canonical JSON Schema subset with canonical structural equality
Named immutable schema identities
Exact serialized-schema byte equality
open_points.default_guess: Use a documented canonical schema subset and compare canonical structural representations.

open_points.subject: Flow inputs and outputs
open_points.text: “A flow is ... a graph” with function and operation nodes; “A flow's own inputs and outputs are values”
open_points.question: How are flow-level input and output ports represented and connected when the only node kinds are function and operation nodes, and what inputs does run a flow accept?
options: Flow versions declare typed boundary ports connected by edges
Special boundary nodes exist but are not counted as executable node kinds
Flows have no caller inputs and outputs are inferred from terminal nodes
open_points.default_guess: Give each flow version explicit typed boundary ports that are not executable nodes.

open_points.subject: Classification of flow inputs
open_points.text: “A flow's own inputs and outputs are values”; “Every value carries open, business_confidential or personal_data.”
open_points.question: Who assigns and validates the disclosure class of caller-supplied flow inputs, and what class do literal or zero-input function outputs receive?
options: Flow input declarations specify a maximum or fixed class and the caller supplies classed values
All caller inputs are personal_data unless proven otherwise
The initiating principal labels each input at run time
open_points.default_guess: Declare classes on flow boundary ports, validate supplied classed values, and classify outputs of executions with no inputs as open.

open_points.subject: Disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “highest class”; “accepting less”
open_points.question: What is the exact ordering and join rule among open, business_confidential and personal_data?
options: open < business_confidential < personal_data with maximum as join
business_confidential and personal_data are incomparable above open
Inputs declare an explicit allowed set rather than an ordering
open_points.default_guess: Use the total order open < business_confidential < personal_data and maximum as the join.

open_points.subject: Map semantics
open_points.text: “a map of a node over a collection”
open_points.question: How does map define element and collection schemas, ordering, concurrency, per-element failures, effect approvals and trace identities?
options: Ordered map with one child execution and trace per element; any failed element fails the map after independent elements finish
Sequential fail-fast map
Unordered bounded-concurrency map with partial results
open_points.default_guess: Use ordered, bounded-concurrency execution with stable per-element trace identities and explicit partial failure.

open_points.subject: Guard semantics
open_points.text: “a guard on a declared closed value”
open_points.question: What supplies the guard value, how branches are represented and proven, what happens for an unmatched value, and how skipped nodes affect outputs and run status?
options: Exhaustive branches over an enum schema; non-selected nodes are skipped
Optional branches with a declared default
A guard conditionally enables one node without requiring exhaustive coverage
open_points.default_guess: Require exhaustive branches over a closed enum and record non-selected nodes as skipped.

open_points.subject: Business facts stored as edge values
open_points.text: “It stores no business fact”; “bounded values that edges carry”; “Values ... are kept for as long as the kernel keeps its traces; this kernel expires nothing.”
open_points.question: May the kernel durably retain edge values that are themselves business facts, or must traces retain only digests while business values are discarded?
options: Retain all bounded edge values indefinitely despite their business meaning
Retain only digests and explicitly designated technical values
Retain values only for the lifetime of the run
open_points.default_guess: Treat “no business fact” as no authoritative business record while still retaining bounded execution values as trace evidence, and state that distinction explicitly.

open_points.subject: Value-size bound
open_points.text: “bounded values that edges carry”; “Traces carry no ... unbounded payload.”
open_points.question: Where are maximum value and diagnostic sizes defined, whether bounds apply before or after encoding, and what observable failure occurs when a service returns too much data?
options: Installation-wide byte ceilings plus optional lower contract bounds
Only per-contract bounds
Per-port schema limits determine all sizes
open_points.default_guess: Apply installation-wide encoded-byte ceilings, allow lower contract limits, and fail the node with a bounded reason on overflow.

open_points.subject: Fixed MCP surface versus listed actions
open_points.text: “one fixed set of typed operations over mcp: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel”
open_points.question: Which MCP operations carry add-trial-case, capture-failure, release-failed-run, rollback-slot, propose-binding, compose-and-prove, and refuse-effect, all of which are primary actions but are not named in the fixed surface?
options: They are distinct operations and must be added to the fixed list
They are explicit subcommands of inspect, author, run or approve
Some are internal transitions and should be removed as caller actions
open_points.default_guess: Define them as typed subcommands under author, run and approve only if that dispatch model is made explicit; otherwise list each operation.

open_points.subject: Meaning of recent repair context
open_points.text: “that slot's recent traces and trial evidence”
open_points.question: What deterministic rule selects “recent” records, and is this context returned by inspect, author, or a separate repair action?
options: Fixed count ordered by record sequence
Fixed time window
All evidence for the current contract version
open_points.default_guess: Return all current-version trial evidence and a fixed, documented count of newest traces via inspect.

open_points.subject: Digest identity and disclosure
open_points.text: “identified by the digest”; “input and output by digest”; “returns the value's digest and class”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and canonical encoding are used for code, records and values, whether domains are separated, and whether personal-data digests are keyed to prevent offline guessing?
options: Domain-separated canonical hashes, with keyed digests for protected values
One unkeyed cryptographic hash over canonical bytes for everything
Opaque store-generated identities unrelated to content hashes
open_points.default_guess: Use domain-separated canonical hashing and a keyed digest for personal-data values exposed to agents.

open_points.subject: Effect send versus store transaction
open_points.text: “A change is one call in one transaction inside the store module”; “only the kernel performs” the external operation
open_points.question: What durable state is committed before and after an HTTP effect so a crash cannot lose the distinction between unsent, sent, known-applied and outcome-unknown?
options: Commit an attempt before sending, then commit the observed outcome in a second transaction
Hold one store transaction open across the HTTP call
Use a transactional outbox or service-side status query
open_points.default_guess: Commit a durable attempt before the send and record the result afterward, treating interruption after send as outcome_unknown.

open_points.subject: Credential changes in approval equality
open_points.text: “the fully built request ... method, URL, headers and body. Any difference at send ... asks again”; “The credential's value is never shown, so rotating it voids nothing.”
open_points.question: Are credential-bearing header values excluded from the approved request identity, despite headers otherwise being covered, and which other installation-injected fields are excluded?
options: Exclude credential values and compare a canonical request with credential placeholders
Include every transmitted header, so credential rotation requires approval again
Approve shown fields only and separately pin all hidden injected fields
open_points.default_guess: Compare a canonical request containing stable credential placeholders and explicitly enumerate all excluded transport fields.
